items.claim: The row correctly holds Eccl.10.2 as a single closed antithetic couplet under the sentence-zone default, with accurate byte and WEB citation.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.10.2 byte text לֵ֤ב חָכָם֙ לִֽימִינ֔וֹ וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִ֖יל לִשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ confirms the symmetric right-hand/left-hand antithesis; the web:Eccl.10.2 quote matches the source verbatim. The rejected alternative (clustering with v.3) is grounded in v.3's distinct narrative-conditional form. No undisclosed catchword bridges either edge: v.2's לב/כסיל/חכם vocabulary does not recur in v.1's dead-flies proverb, and the couplet is grammatically complete in itself.

items.claim: The row correctly holds Eccl.10.3 as a standalone single_saying, properly discloses the inline ketiv/qere, and honestly names then reasonably rejects the shared heart/fool vocabulary with v.2 as common book-wide terms rather than a deliberate repeated construction.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.10.3 byte text carries the ketiv כשהסכל beside the qere כְּשֶׁסָּכָ֥ל, matching the pmarks kq inventory entry at MT 10:3; the web:Eccl.10.3 quote is verbatim. Note v.2's כסיל and v.3's סכל are in fact two different Hebrew lexemes, not the identical root the row's prose loosely calls a 'fool-root' — but since the row uses this shared vocabulary only to REJECT clustering (as common, not construction-level), the imprecision does not change the correct boundary conclusion; if anything it strengthens the row's own point.

items.claim: The row correctly treats Eccl.10.4 as one grammatical sentence and properly discloses the imperative clause as an operative-category deviation rather than promoting it to admonition_unit.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.10.4 byte text is a single conditional sentence (protasis אִם ר֤וּחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁל֙ תַּעֲלֶ֣ה עָלֶ֔יךָ, apodosis מְקוֹמְךָ֖ אַל תַּנַּ֑ח, rationale כִּ֣י מַרְפֵּ֔א יַנִּ֖יחַ חֲטָאִ֥ים גְּדוֹלִֽים). No catchword bridges it to v.3 (fool/heart vocabulary absent here) or to v.5 (v.4's הַמּוֹשֵׁל֙ is a different root than v.5's הַשַּׁלִּֽיט, and v.4 carries none of v.5's tachat-hashemesh or ראיתי markers), so no undisclosed cross-seam cohesion threatens either edge. The WEB quotes match the source verbatim.

items.claim: The saying_cluster call for Eccl.10.5-10.6 is adequately byte-grounded: v.6 opens asyndetically as apposition, and the cluster is correctly bounded against v.7's fresh, independently-headed observation.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.10.6 byte text נִתַּ֣ן הַסֶּ֔כֶל בַּמְּרוֹמִ֖ים רַבִּ֑ים... opens with no leading vav, consistent with reading it as apposition specifying the unnamed 'error' (כִּשְׁגָגָ֕ה) closing v.5. v.7's own byte text רָאִ֥יתִי עֲבָדִ֖ים עַל סוּסִ֑ים... reopens the ראיתי observation-formula independently; the device inventory's raiti_observations list carries both Eccl.10.5 and Eccl.10.7 as separate sites (18 verses book-wide), supporting the row's exclusion of v.7. Confidence is appropriately held at medium given the asyndeton-only basis.

items.claim: The row correctly isolates Eccl.10.7 as a fresh single_saying on the strength of its own independent ראיתי observation-opener, consistent with how that formula functions at its other book-wide sites.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.10.7 byte text opens רָאִ֥יתִי עֲבָדִ֖ים עַל סוּסִ֑ים with no continuing conjunction from v.6. The device inventory's raiti_observations list (18 sites total) treats each occurrence, including Eccl.10.5 and Eccl.10.7, as its own discrete observation elsewhere in the book, supporting the row's atomic call over a v.5-7 megacluster. The WEB quote is verbatim.

items.claim: The saying_cluster call for Eccl.10.8-10.9 is well-grounded in a genuine four-fold matched grammatical template (participle-subject plus resumptive-pronoun harm-clause) across both verses' cola, correctly bounded before v.10's shift to a conditional form.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.10.8 (חֹפֵ֥ר גּוּמָּ֖ץ בּ֣וֹ יִפּ֑וֹל; וּפֹרֵ֥ץ גָּדֵ֖ר יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ נָחָֽשׁ) and oshb:Eccl.10.9 (מַסִּ֣יעַ אֲבָנִ֔ים יֵעָצֵ֖ב בָּהֶ֑ם; בּוֹקֵ֥עַ עֵצִ֖ים יִסָּ֥כֶן בָּֽם) byte-confirm the same participle+harm-verb+pronominal-object pattern across all four cola, a stronger construction-level basis than a shared-theme claim. The template genuinely does not extend to v.10, which shifts to an אִם-conditional form, so the row's far boundary is sound.

items.claim: The saying_cluster call for Eccl.10.10-10.11 overstates a keyword bracket that is actually Qohelet's own habitual thematic vocabulary, and omits a genuine, undisclosed cross-seam echo tying v.11 back to v.8 inside the preceding row's own span.
items.evidence: The row's sole named cohesion, יתרון, is not a locally distinctive device: a skeleton sweep of יתרון returns 9 verses book-wide (Eccl.1.3, 2.11, 2.13, 3.9, 5.8=web5.9, 5.15=web5.16, 7.12, 10.10, 10.11) — it is Qohelet's own recurring profit/advantage vocabulary, not a marker unique to this pair, which risks the 'shared theme dressed as shared keyword' pattern the owner ruling treats as over-clustering. The token is also not verse-final in either verse: oshb:Eccl.10.10 continues past וְיִתְר֥וֹן to הכשיר הַכְשֵׁ֖ר חָכְמָֽה (two more tokens), and oshb:Eccl.10.11 continues past וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן to לְבַ֖עַל הַלָּשֽׁוֹן (two more tokens) — so the row's 'closes with'/'brackets both endings' framing overstates the token's structural position; it sits within, not at, each verse's final clause. Separately, oshb:Eccl.10.8 (in the preceding row's own span) closes וּפֹרֵ֥ץ גָּדֵ֖ר יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ נָחָֽשׁ, and oshb:Eccl.10.11 (this row's own opening) reads אִם יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ הַנָּחָ֖שׁ — both share the same 'bite' verb (v.8's יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ, Qal imperfect+3ms suffix; v.11's יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ, Qal imperfect) immediately beside נחש/הנחש ('snake'), a byte-true echo bracketing the whole v.8-11 hazard run that neither this row nor its neighbor discloses, and that argues for real continuity across the v.9|v.10 seam this row treats as closed. The K/Q at oshb:Eccl.10.10 (הכשיר/הַכְשֵׁ֖ר) is itself correctly disclosed against the pmarks inventory, and confidence is already honestly held at medium_low; the challenge is that the named cohesion is thinner, and the undisclosed counter-evidence larger, than the row discloses.

items.claim: The saying_cluster call for Eccl.10.12-10.13 rests on a genuinely rare, book-wide-unique repeated construct phrase plus a sound pronominal-chaining argument, and correctly excludes v.14.
items.evidence: A skeleton sweep of the exact phrase דברי פי returns only Eccl.10.12 and Eccl.10.13 book-wide, confirming the repetition (opening דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי in v.12, resumed with a suffix as דִּבְרֵי פִ֖יהוּ in v.13) is a locally distinctive device rather than habitual vocabulary. The pronominal 'his' in v.13 correctly resumes כְּסִ֖יל named near the end of v.12. v.14's וְהַסָּכָ֖ל יַרְבֶּ֣ה דְבָרִ֑ים uses plain דברים, not the construct דברי פי, so the row's exclusion of v.14 is byte-accurate rather than theme-driven. WEB quotes are verbatim.
